requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured to run a DHCP server on the private network (eth1) shared with node2/node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 was assigned static 10.50.50.254/24 and a kea-dhcp4 shared-network/subnet config (authoritative, subnet-id, range 10.50.50.100-200, default-router, name-server, lease) was committed and saved to /config/config.boot. Post-commit verification shows kea-dhcp4 actively listening on 10.50.50.254:67 on eth1, and this state persisted through a full node1 reboot (socket and config both recovered post-restart).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain their private-network address from node1 via DHCP rather than static assignment
requirements.summary: node2/node3's enp8s0 NM profiles were confirmed set to ipv4.method=auto (not static). After bringing the connection up, node2 leased 10.50.50.101 and node3 leased 10.50.50.100 from node1's DHCP server, and both re-acquired the same leases after a full reboot of each node.

requirements.requirement: Cross-node connectivity across the private DHCP network functions end-to-end
requirements.summary: node1 successfully pinged both leased addresses (10.50.50.100 and 10.50.50.101) both before and after the full restart cycle of all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state for all three nodes
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state snapshot was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged, polling confirmed a distinct post-restart boot_id, and service/data state recovered (node1: kea-dhcp4 process and eth1 address restored; node2/node3: same DHCP lease re-acquired). The fixed lifecycle before_prepare/after_executor snapshots independently corroborate the boot_id changes and the appearance of the kea-dhcp4 listening socket on node1.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied: node1 runs an authoritative kea-dhcp4 server on its private-network interface, node2 and node3 acquire their private-network addresses dynamically from it rather than statically, and cross-node connectivity works. The executor additionally ran the full node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes with clean before/ack/changed-boot-id/recovered evidence for each, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: The DHCP lease list/database on node1 (kea leases file) was not directly inspected - recovery was verified via socket state, process presence, and successful client re-leasing rather than a leases-file dump.

node2/node3's ipv4.method=auto setting pre-existed the executor's changes (visible before any node1 DHCP configuration), so the executor's contribution for those nodes was primarily activating the connection and verifying the lease rather than changing the NM profile itself; this does not affect the satisfied outcome but is noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary or lingering mutations were identified. The one failed VyOS commit attempt (cmd-7bafd858e1394ba9, using an incorrect subnet-parameters/default-router/name-server syntax) did not persist any state - the commit failed and VyOS explicitly warned that uncommitted changes would not be saved - so it is a corrective discovery step rather than a residual mutation. Other non-zero-exit commands (cmd-2deeb6295e4e451f 'show' not found, connection-reset/timeout polls during the three reboots) are expected transient effects of read-only diagnostics or the reboot windows themselves, not state changes. The three reboots (cmd-d006117b377f4d24, cmd-983a18533ac84961, cmd-3f459ce5dee44b12) were required by the mandatory restart protocol and were fully recovered. Lifecycle diffs show only expected boot-id-tied churn (systemd-private tmp dirs, ephemeral high ports) and the intended new kea-dhcp4 listening socket on node1; no failed services, package damage, or unsafe exposure appeared in any node's before/after comparison.
